headline.purpose: Section titles (h2). 36px, scaling to 28/25px on small screens.

body.purpose: Default prose at 17px/1.6; long-form articles step to 18px/1.75, capped 70–74ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase eyebrows, kickers, table headers; 12.5px, 0.12–0.14em tracking, often with a leading dot.

shadows.purpose: KPI and overview cards at rest — soft green lift plus crisp hairline.

shadows.name: card-hover

shadows.name: frame

shadows.name: header-seam

narrative.overview:
This is the authoritative, map-first record of who in Nigeria has power and who does not. It should feel like opening the definitive national reference — official, but never cold. The visual world is built from two things the platform actually traffics in: land (a deep forest-green cover, the colour of the country's electrification mission) and data layers (clean white plates that lift off the page, maps that carry the eye, numbers set in confident type). Dark green establishes authority at the top of every page; a light, almost paper-white body carries the evidence below it.

The system runs on restraint. One typeface (Inter) does all the work; one green carries nearly all the brand weight; depth is gentle and functional. Against that calm institutional base, a single bright mint is the spark — used sparingly, mostly on dark grounds, to mark what's live, what's current, what matters now. Sector work is colour-coded with discipline: slate-blue for the power sector, amber for solar home systems, mint for mini-grids and the default. These are signals, not decoration.

The platform serves developers, government planners, DisCos, researchers and students together, often on mobile and on variable Nigerian networks. So the craft shows as precision and legibility: generous line length, tabular numerals on every statistic, honest sourcing lines under charts, and interactions that reward without distracting. Nothing here is loud for its own sake. The confidence comes from clarity.
keyCharacteristics: Deep forest-green authority bands over a light, paper-white body.
One typeface (Inter), hierarchy built from size, weight and tracking.
Flat pages; white cards float on soft green-tinted shadows and lift on hover.
A single bright mint accent, used rarely, as the 'live / now' signal.
Disciplined sector colour-coding: slate = power, amber = solar, leaf = mini-grid/default.
Map, data-layer and chart motifs as the recurring visual language.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: REA Green (#006438) is the only accent that appears freely on light surfaces. Everything else — leaf, slate, amber — is reserved for a specific job. If you reach for a second colour 'to add interest,' stop: use green, or use white space.

rules.name: The Live-Mint Rule
rules.body: Bright Mint (#C8F0C8) is the 'now' signal, not a fill. It belongs to pulsing status dots, hero highlight words, focus rings, and the leaf CTA on dark bands — surfaces where it reads as energy. It should never become a large flat background on a light page.

rules.name: The Sector Signal Rule
rules.body: Slate = power sector, amber = solar home systems, mint = mini-grids and the default. A sector colour appears only to mark that sector's content (a chip, a dot, a page accent bar). It is never decoration and never mixed across sectors.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Inter is the entire type system. Never introduce a second family for 'contrast' — contrast comes from weight (400 vs 600/700), size, and tracking. A serif or display face would break the institutional voice.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every figure that represents data — KPIs, stats, file sizes, years, chart labels — uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so columns align and numbers don't jitter between states.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest unless they are a distinct floating object (a card, a menu, a frame). Shadows signal 'this is a separate thing' or respond to hover/focus — they are never applied to sections, bands, or text blocks for ambience.

rules.name: The Green-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Card and UI shadows are tinted with rgba(0,61,34,…) (midnight pine), not black. Reserve neutral-black shadow only for mockup frames sitting on dark grounds.

dos: Do lead with REA Green (#006438) for all primary action and brand emphasis on light surfaces; let white space do the rest.
Do reserve bright Mint (#C8F0C8) for 'live/now' signals, hero highlights, focus rings, and the CTA on dark bands — small doses only.
Do key sector content with its signal colour (slate = power, amber = solar, leaf = mini-grid/default) and nothing else.
Do tint card shadows with rgba(0,61,34,…), and pair every hover lift with a matching translateY.
Do set every data figure in Inter with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
Do keep long-form reading to 70–74ch and step body type up to 18px/1.75 in articles.
Do give every interactive element a 3px focus outline: REA Green (#006438) on light surfaces, Mint only on dark green grounds. WCAG 2.2 AA requires a 3:1 focus indicator, and leaf-on-white is ~1.6:1.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion (reveals and loops already disable under it).
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface — build contrast from Inter's weights, sizes, and tracking.
Don't add a new accent colour 'for variety'; the palette is deliberately narrow.
Don't flood a light surface with a large flat mint fill — it's a spark, not a background.
Don't use neutral-black shadows on light surfaces (green-tinted only); reserve black shadow for mockup frames on dark grounds.
Don't apply shadows to sections, bands, or text blocks for ambience — depth belongs to discrete floating objects.
Don't add new eyebrow/kicker labels above headings or new left-edge accent bars — both are legacy; retain existing instances but don't extend the pattern.

Don't reference 'SE4ALL' or the global SEforALL initiative to describe the platform; keep REA as the primary brand with the Federal Ministry of Power as policy partner. (Historical blog/event names stay as published.)
